trust_decision.summary: Whether caller-supplied bytes (a value under reject_bytes=False, or any bytes dict key) are well-formed UTF-8 before being re-emitted as \uXXXX escapes under ensure_ascii=True; decided only in Buffer_EscapeStringValidated (lead-byte length, overlong checks; no continuation-byte, no >U+10FFFF check, off-by-one truncation check). The ensure_ascii=False and __json__ raw paths copy bytes verbatim and are backstopped by the final PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8(surrogatepass).

landing_point.why: Summary names ujson.dumps() and UTF-8 validation of bytes; Buffer_EscapeStringValidated is the only encoder function with UTF-8 sequence errors ('Unterminated UTF-8 sequence', 'Overlong ...'), found by grepping the error strings.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Published behavioural change is confined to one function, Buffer_EscapeStringValidated (src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c:302-452), shared by the key path (src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c:690-696) and the value path (src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c:906-914); decoder edits are message text only.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory title is about ujson.dumps(); the decoder's own UTF-8 parser in loads() is the opposite direction, has its own 'Invalid octet' check that looks like validation (src/ujson/lib/ultrajsondec.c:529-532), and the published fix only renamed its messages, so a solver can argue loads() is out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: UTF-8-encoded lone surrogates in bytes (b'\xed\xa0\x80') and in str (encoded with surrogatepass) must keep encoding to \ud800-style escapes; a fix that swaps in strict UTF-8 decoding or rejects ED A0-BF breaks this. Also lone surrogates must keep round-tripping through loads.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ujson.loads(bytes) decoder accepts a non-continuation byte (0xC0-0xFF) as continuation because it tests only bit 0x80, and silently rewrites the sequence to a different code point.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Advisory names dumps(); decoder already has an 'Invalid octet' check and the fix only touched its messages.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: sibling file in same directory (src/ujson/lib/ultrajsondec.c vs ultrajsonenc.c); reached via src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c:204-216

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ujson.loads(bytes) decoder maps a lone continuation byte 0x80-0xBF through the 1-byte case, yielding U+0080-U+00BF instead of an error (only 0xF8-0xFF are table errors).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Looks like deliberate Latin-1-style passthrough; the dumps side relies on a final decode at src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c:867 for the same bytes, and loads has no such backstop.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ujson.loads(bytes) decoder 4-byte case has no >U+10FFFF check (leads F4 90+ and F5-F7 are accepted by the table).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Probably surfaces as an exception from PyUnicode_FromKindAndData (src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c:84) rather than silent rewrite, so it can be argued harmless.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Validate bytes dict keys in Dict_convertKey with a separate (weaker) check rather than in the shared escape function, so a key-only route stays open.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Keys already get their own conversion and ignore reject_bytes; a maintainer adding key handling (e.g. sort_keys) could plausibly add a local check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A __json__/raw-bytes path that skips the final decode (e.g. a bytes-returning dumps variant) so raw invalid UTF-8 escapes the backstop at src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c:867.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Returning bytes directly to avoid the final UTF-8 decode is a common performance request for JSON libraries.
